title: Spec a story, then plan the retest of a change
prompt: Two things for our checkout team. First, write the acceptance criteria for this story: As a customer, I want to apply a promo code at checkout so that I pay less. A code can be used once per customer. An expired code shows "This code has expired." Gift cards are out of scope. Second, we shipped this change yesterday: promo codes now apply before shipping is calculated, and the old Coupon link in the footer is removed. What should we retest after that change?
agent: claude -p in an empty project outside the repository, with spec-writer, test-planner installed
answer:
## Acceptance criteria: apply a promo code at checkout

Requirement: A customer can apply a promo code at checkout to pay less, each code can be used once per customer, and an expired code shows a stated message.

### Main path
AC-1. Given a customer at checkout, when the customer applies a promo code, then the amount the customer pays is less than before the code was applied. _I want to apply a promo code at checkout so that I pay less_

### Validation and errors
AC-2. Given an expired code, when the customer applies it at checkout, then the message "This code has expired." is shown. _An expired code shows "This code has expired."_

### Limits
AC-3. Given a customer who has already used a code once, when that customer applies the same code again, then the code is not applied. _A code can be used once per customer._

### Open questions
- Main path: By how much does an applied promo code reduce the amount the customer pays?
- Main path: What does the customer see at checkout once a promo code has been applied?
- Validation and errors: What is shown when a customer applies a code they have already used?
- Validation and errors: What is shown when a customer applies a code that does not exist?
- Validation and errors: What happens to the amount to pay when an expired code is applied?
- Permissions and roles: Who other than a customer may apply a promo code?
- Empty, loading and disabled states: What is shown at checkout before any promo code is applied?
- Persistence after reload: What happens to an applied promo code when the customer reloads checkout?
- Limits: What event counts as a code being used?
- Limits: How is a customer identified for the once-per-customer rule?
- Limits: How many promo codes can a customer apply to one order?

### Out of scope
- Gift cards. _Gift cards are out of scope._

---

## Regression checklist: promo codes before shipping, Coupon link removed

Change: Promo codes now apply before shipping is calculated, and the old Coupon link in the footer is removed.

### promo codes
1. [ ] Apply a promo code and check the code is applied before shipping is calculated. _promo codes now apply before shipping is calculated_

### footer
2. [ ] Open the footer and check the old Coupon link no longer appears. _the old Coupon link in the footer is removed_

### Possible impact, not stated
- Does the order total at checkout still add up when a promo code and shipping are both present? The change text does not name it.
- Do free-shipping thresholds still behave as intended when a promo code lowers the order total? The change text does not name it.
- Is tax still calculated on the intended amount now that the order of calculation has changed? The change text does not name it.
- Do order confirmations, emails and invoices show the same totals as checkout? The change text does not name it.
- Do refunds and partial returns on orders with a promo code still give the intended amounts? The change text does not name it.
- Is the page the Coupon link pointed to still reachable, and do any other links to it still work? The change text does not name it.

### Open questions
- Does the shipping cost itself change when a promo code lowers the order total, or only the order of calculation?
- Do promo codes that affect shipping (if any exist) still apply now that codes run before shipping is calculated?
- What, if anything, replaces the Coupon link, and where should customers who used it go now?
